why: The vocabulary a realtime message uses to say what it is. Read by a Go test and a vitest test, so a kind added on one side without the other turns the other side red.

families.why: A change to a document the account can see, carrying the document and its collection. A message that names no type is this family: every producer of document changes predates the field.
Something happened that a client may want to react to. Carries no document and no collection, so it can never be routed by the document dispatch.

subtypes.why: An owner's archived-job statistics have been written. Carries the owner and a timestamp and no figures: the client refreshes what it is displaying rather than being sent figures it may not be showing.

families.why: The stack entered a maintenance window. Carries enabled and a message and is sent to every connected client immediately before its socket is closed, so the client shows the banner rather than reading the close as a failure. Leaving a window sends nothing: no client is connected to tell.

A new Static Data Export build was published. Carries the build number and version and goes to every connected client regardless of who is signed in, because the files are the same for all of them. The client compares the build against the one it holds and refreshes its cache only if it has moved.

Who is holding, waiting for or viewing a document. Delivered to the tabs of the account that owns it, less the session that caused it: a viewer joining or leaving is one fact about a whole session rather than about one tab. Its kinds travel in an `event` field of the frame rather than in a subtype, so it lists none here.
